recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Sun Dog, Moon Cat and Luck", "body": "Jaz explained that he and a friend invented two spirits, Sun Dog as the spirit of luck and Moon Cat as the prankster of misfortune. He said Moon Cat knocked things over and laughed when people got angry, while Sun Dog arrived once a person laughed along. Jaz told of a mishap at work, a hole punched through a screen door, where owning up to it led to an unexpected favor. Chance compared Sun Dog to Falcor, the luck dragon from The Neverending Story, and said Jaz had accidentally stumbled upon metaphysics."}, {"title": "Flow, Control and the Ego", "body": "Chance described the torus, a donut shaped flow of energy, and argued that trying to control the outside world left people stuck and pushed backward, while letting go carried them back to the center. Jaz used the image of a pinky finger trying to dig a gold mine alone to argue that the ego was only a small part of a person. The talk then turned to manifestation, and the pair agreed that aiming at a feeling rather than one exact outcome left room for something better than a person could plan."}, {"title": "Memory, Ego States and Personas", "body": "Chance argued from his work with tuning forks in the biofield that memories were not stored in the brain, and he said experiences a person could not face were pushed out into the field. He described ego states, versions of a person from a past period, and said a repressed version could persist as an entity in a psychic realm. Jaz asked whether someone could enjoy having multiple personalities, and the talk settled on the idea that persona means mask and that the question was how authentic the mask was."}, {"title": "Breath, Sungazing and Imagination", "body": "Jaz described Wim Hof breathing, thirty deep breaths followed by a long breath hold, and claimed it raised adrenaline while lowering cortisol. He warned against trying it while driving. Chance asked Jaz about sungazing, and Jaz described strobing sunlight through closed eyelids and suggested a cheap yard pinwheel to speed the effect. Chance recounted a walk where he and a friend both saw a sungazing stranger appear to turn blue, and the conversation turned to imagination producing real bodily sensations."}, {"title": "Psychedelic Visions and Video Game Lessons", "body": "Jaz said that at nineteen his Xbox failed during a trip and he then saw a dark figure dancing by the water at sunrise, after which he traveled for years. He described a later large psilocybin trip with a figure in a cowboy hat, a Jesus and devil argument, and a swap between being small and being large. He said the trip told him to return to video games, and that gaming later showed him his ego getting in the way, since letting go of control sometimes let him pass levels on the first try."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: My homie Jaz the Wrapper joins me for episode 1 of Vibe Rant, the very first night of my brand new show.
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "When I started out InnerVerse, a lot of the people I talked to were generally just friends and artists, and maybe they didn't even have an internet presence or there was no serious business to dive into.
